title: Build Dynamic Products, and Stop the AI Sideshow — Eliza Cabrera (Workday) + Jeremy Silva (Freeplay)
talk_summary: A product-management talk from Workday and Freeplay arguing that AI features should be deeply integrated into product strategy rather than bolted on as an 'AI sideshow', illustrated with a crawl/walk/run maturity model for Workday's HR help product. It contains no engineering mechanisms, measurements, or agent-orchestration techniques.

takeaways.technique: Crawl/walk/run staging of AI capability rollout
takeaways.what_they_do: They sequence AI capability in three stages: crawl = AI on the backend accentuating existing functionality with no new surface area; walk = contextual/personalized features with some new surface area; run = autonomous agents operating across the product suite requiring UX/architecture rework, with each stage building on the last rather than replacing it.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you're not throwing out functionality. It's building on top of each other. It's that functionality is building as you go
